vol_regime_judgement: 13.2% annualised realised vol is ~0.83% daily. I do NOT read that as a hard cap on the post-print move: the tape itself shows $0.97 -> $1.02 in two sessions (2026-09-03/04), a 5.2% two-day move, so a marginal buyer can move this name 5% when one shows up. What the low vol plus the reaction record DOES say is narrower and more damaging to the fundamental claims: seven distinct prior prints, max absolute reaction 3.33%, and specifically -1.20% on the 2026-03-25 print that revealed +105.5% revenue and +RMB637.8m of new technical service income, and +2.34% on the 2026-06-17 print that revealed +64.8% revenue with S&M tripling. The market declined to move on the arrival of the entire revenue-mix story in either direction. So for WDH#0 and WDH#1 the operative objection is not 'the information is impounded' but 'this price does not respond to income-statement composition', which for a horizon of the close after the print is the same answer. For WDH#3 and WDH#4 the low vol cuts the other way: they are about capital flow and a mechanical threshold into a book that turns ~$255k a day, and flow does move this tape - which is why those two get lower priced_in numbers than the fundamentals claims despite resting on older public documents.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every component number is correct and every one of them is lifted from two press releases that went out on the full PR Newswire APAC wire and were carried by Morningstar, Yahoo, AOL, Manila Times, Macau Business, StockTitan and TipRanks. Technical service income RMB1.8m/9.4m/639.6m/421.0m checks out; insurance-related income 1,145.8 less 421.0 gives brokerage 724.8, and 658.0 less 9.4 gives 648.7, so +11.7% YoY is right; 1,310.4 less 639.6 gives 670.8; net profit RMB98.4m vs RMB108.2m is a line in the release. The only error is cosmetic: S&M was 43.5% of revenue, not 43.6%. What makes this priced is not the subtraction, which I could not find headlined anywhere, but the implication: TipRanks' 2026-06-16 note already said operating profit rose only 5.3% 'despite a sharp increase in sales and marketing spend'; management stated on the public Q1 call that 'operating profit scale is expected to remain broadly stable' in 2026 against roughly 40% revenue growth, which is them telling the market in advance that the revenue line is not flowing through; and the published estimate track already shows FY26 revenue revised UP from CN¥4.04b to CN¥4.56b while EPS was cut from CN¥1.46 to CN¥1.19 - the exact shape of this finding, already in the numbers people quote. Held at 70 rather than 85 only because the 'brokerage income +11.7%' figure itself is genuinely absent from all coverage I could find.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Discloses technical service income of RMB639.6m in Q4 2025 against RMB1.8m in Q4 2024, and insurance-related income of RMB1,310.4m, from which brokerage income of RMB670.8m follows by subtraction.
Q1 2026 release: technical service income RMB421.0m vs RMB9.4m, insurance-related income RMB1,145.8m vs RMB658.0m, S&M RMB541.1m at 43.5% of revenue vs 22.9%, net profit RMB98.4m vs RMB108.2m.
Wire-level coverage stating operating profit rose only 5.3% to RMB80.0m despite a sharp increase in sales and marketing spend - the 'growth is not flowing through' point, in print on the day.
Q1 2026 call transcript: management guides operating profit scale to remain broadly stable in 2026 against roughly 40% revenue growth, and confirms S&M nearly tripled to CNY541m.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The two prints that actually delivered this story are both in the baseline's move list and neither moved the stock: 2026-03-25 (Q4 2025, technical service income appearing from nothing, revenue +105.5%) printed -1.20%, and 2026-06-17 (Q1 2026, revenue +64.8%, S&M to 43.5%, net profit down) printed +2.34%. A market that would not sell -9.1% net profit on the day it was reported is not going to re-rate on the subtraction that explains it.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A Q2 print showing technical service income falling a second consecutive quarter AND brokerage income going outright negative YoY, which would break management's own 40%-revenue/stable-profit frame rather than confirm it.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The underlying data is entirely public and in wire copy: GlobeNewswire 2026-08-20, plus Yahoo, TipRanks, Quiver, Manila Times and a full Benzinga transcript. I reproduced the ratio - 719.8/4,196.4 = 17.15% against 680.5/3,233.7 = 21.05%, an 18.5% relative decline - so the arithmetic is right and the derivation is two divisions away from a press release. What holds this at 50 rather than higher is that nobody drew the ratio and nobody connected it to Waterdrop; the Huize coverage was uniformly positive ('Record Premiums and Profit Surge'), so the compression reading is not the told narrative. What holds it at 50 rather than lower is three factual objections to the claim as framed, which I state separately from pricing. First, 'exactly the April-June window' is wrong: this is a half-year report and you cannot isolate Q2 from it - half of the compression sits in Jan-Mar, a period Waterdrop has already reported. Second, revenue/GWP is not a take rate: GWP includes renewal premium that carries little incremental revenue, and Huize's FYP grew 48.7% into savings product where first-year commission is structurally far below long-term health protection, so a falling ratio is substantially a mix effect, not a rate cut. Third, the transmission channel to Waterdrop is weak by Waterdrop's own construction - 34% of its revenue is now technical service income, which is not premium commission at all.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Huize H1 2026: GWP RMB4,196.4m +29.8%, FYP RMB2,763.0m +48.7%, operating revenue RMB719.8m +5.8% - every input to the claimed ratio, on the wire.
Same-day coverage framing the result positively on record premiums and rising net profit - evidence the compression reading was NOT the published narrative.

Sector-level reporting that the 'reporting-and-conduct integration' regime and July 2026 bancassurance expense rules have already cut commission rates across channels - i.e. the compression driver is a published, sector-wide, known fact rather than a company discovery.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: None on the WDH tape. WDH's 20-day run-up is +2.0% and its 5-day is +2.7%; there is no visible mark-down around 2026-08-20. But there is also no analyst and no option chain through which a peer read-across could be discounted, so the absence of a move is uninformative rather than exculpatory. The relevant baseline fact is the reaction record: WDH did not move on its own take-rate compression when it reported it.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A Huize disclosure isolating Q2 from H1 and showing the ratio decline steepening into April-June specifically, or a Waterdrop Q2 release showing brokerage income down sequentially as well as barely up YoY.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Both 'exits' are in wire copy with dated URLs and one of them has its own dedicated explainer article published a month before this print. The Feng resignation and the Qianfei Chang audit-chair appointment went out on PR Newswire on 2026-06-23 and were picked up by Nasdaq, TipRanks, Investing.com and Pluang the same day. The Xu resignation was 6-K'd on 2026-07-24, covered by TipRanks that day, and then written up at length by Simply Wall St and syndicated to Yahoo Finance on 2026-08-06 under the headline 'What Does Waterdrop's Finance Chief Exit Reveal About Its AI Investment Priorities?' - which is precisely this finding, published, thirty-two days before the print. The CFO vacancy dates to June 2022 and has been disclosed in four consecutive 20-Fs; age is not novelty. Separately, three of the claim's factual assertions do not survive checking. (i) 'No head of finance' is wrong or at least badly overstated: the very 6-K cited is signed by Jieru Li as 'Vice President of Finance, Board Secretary and Head of Strategy and Capital Markets', and the published coverage read her role as continuity in financial leadership. (ii) 'The FY2025 20-F carrying the undisclosed RMB639.6m revenue line' is wrong: RMB639.6m was disclosed by name in the Q4 2025 press release of 2026-03-25 and carried on the wire - and finding WDH#0 in this same brief correctly cites it as disclosed. (iii) Feng resigned as an independent director outright, not merely from three committees, and his replacement as audit chair was named in the same release on the same day, which is an orderly succession rather than a gap.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Announces Heping Feng's resignation as independent director and from the audit, compensation and nominating committees, and the appointment of Qianfei Chang as independent director and audit committee chair effective 2026-07-01.
Same-day wire coverage of Xiaoying Xu's resignation as VP of Finance and Head of Finance effective 2026-07-31.

A dedicated syndicated analysis of the finance-chief exit, explicitly tying it to the buyback and semiannual dividend and to 'balancing shareholder payouts with heavy AI investment' - the finding's own thesis, in print, a month before the print.
Nasdaq carriage of the same board-reshuffle release, confirming general distribution.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The baseline's own move list contains both dates and neither shows adverse reaction: 2026-06-23 (the Feng/Chang 6-K) printed -0.83%, and 2026-07-24 (the Xu resignation 6-K) printed +2.68% - the largest up-move in the recorded series happened on the day the head of finance quit. Whatever the market made of these filings, it did not sell them.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A Q2 filing that is late, unreviewed, or carries a material-weakness or auditor-change disclosure, which would convert governance turnover from noise into an event.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The forward mechanical fact is real and I verified all of it - the $50m authorisation was approved 2025-09-02, announced on PR Newswire 2025-09-04, expressly runs 'during the 12-month period through September 9, 2026', cumulative repurchase ran $109.0m at 2025-08-31 to $120.1m at 2026-05-31 so roughly four-fifths is unused, and there have been five consecutive September programmes since 2021 with $0.03/ADS dividends attached to Q2 2025. But three things make it substantially priced. First, the expiry date is not obscure: it is stated in the company's own release and repeated in the FY2025 20-F, both a year old, and the 2026-08-06 Yahoo/Simply Wall St piece went into this print discussing the buyback and semiannual dividends as the capital-return frame. Second, five-for-five is a base rate, not news - this is 'structural and known', and the market has watched the identical announcement arrive on the Q2 print in each of 2024 and 2025. Third and most damaging, the flow is arguably already in the tape: the stock went $0.97 to $1.02 on 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-04, a 5.2% two-day move on a name with 0.83% daily vol and $255k of daily turnover, in the last two sessions before an authorisation with roughly $39m of unused capacity expires on 2026-09-09. That is exactly what company buying into an expiry looks like, and it is the baseline's entire +2.72% five-day run-up. So the mechanism reaches the print but part of it has already been paid for. Not higher than 60 because no one has written down 'expect a new authorisation on September 8', there is no option chain to express it, and no analyst to publish it.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Announces the fifth repurchase programme, up to US$50m during the 12-month period through September 9, 2026, alongside a US$0.03/ADS dividend, and notes four prior programmes since September 2021.
FY2025 20-F repeats the September 2025 programme's US$50m size and its expiry through September 9, 2026, and gives usage to date.
Cites 5,278,431 shares repurchased for about US$9.54m by 2026-05-31 and frames the buyback plus semiannual dividends as the live capital-return question going into this print.
The prior year's identical pattern - Q2 results plus a special cash dividend announced on the September Q2 print - establishing the base rate as public and repeated.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Two things. The precedent: 2025-09-04, the Q2 print that carried the new $50m authorisation and a 50%-raised dividend, printed +2.25%, the second-largest up-move in the recorded series - so this specific announcement is empirically the one thing that has moved this name, and it is worth about 2%. And the run-up: +2.72% over five days, essentially all of it the $0.97-to-$1.02 bounce on the two sessions immediately before the print, which on a 0.83%-daily-vol name is a six-sigma two-day move and is most parsimoniously explained by the expiring authorisation being used.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: The programme lapsing on 2026-09-09 with no successor announced on the print, or a Q2 release that omits the dividend - either would make the finding wrong rather than priced.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I reproduced the computation independently and every number is right, which is worth stating because it is unusual. The 30 trading sessions from 2026-07-27 to 2026-09-04 are exactly 30 (the summariser I used dropped 2026-08-24, a normal Monday session; Labor Day 2026 is 09-07, after the window). Summing the closes with 08-24 at $0.99 gives $30.79 and an average of $1.02633 - the claim's $1.0263 is correct to four decimals. The five sessions rolling out closed $1.15/$1.15/$1.15/$1.14/$1.12 for $5.71, leaving $25.08, so the next five closes must sum to $4.92, an average of $0.984, which is 3.5% below the $1.02 spot. I searched for an NYSE 802.01C notice and for any published version of this arithmetic and found neither, so the computation is genuinely not out - that is why this is not 70. What stops it being 15 is that the boundary itself is manifestly in the tape already: WDH closed at exactly $1.00 on thirteen consecutive sessions from 2026-08-05 through 2026-08-21, then $0.99 for five, then $0.97, then bounced to $1.02 immediately before the print. A three-week pin at precisely the listing threshold on a stock that turns $255k a day is not coincidence; the $1.00 line is being watched and defended, and the defence is the baseline's own run-up. Beyond that, the mechanism does not reach the horizon being measured and is directionally backwards from how such a finding usually reads: 802.01C produces a notice and a six-month cure period, not a delisting, and is routinely cured by an ADS ratio change; and a company with roughly $39m of unused repurchase authorisation expiring the day after the print has both the means and the motive to hold the line. The compliance boundary here is a floor argument, not a downside catalyst, and nothing about it resolves at the close after this print.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The public daily close series the computation runs over, including the run of exact $1.00 closes from 2026-08-05 and the $0.97 to $1.02 bounce on 09-03/09-04.
Automated coverage noting WDH traded as high as $1.01 and last traded at $1.00 in mid-August - the sub-dollar proximity was being written about, even if the 30-day average was not.

Background on the NYSE/Nasdaq minimum price regime: the 30-trading-day average test triggers a notice and a cure period, not immediate delisting - the reason the mechanism does not resolve inside this print's window.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The whole of the baseline tape is the evidence. Spot $1.02 with pct_from_52w_low of only +4.83%, realised vol of 13.2% annualised, and a +2.72% five-day run-up that is entirely the last two sessions - a stock pinned at $1.00 for three weeks and then bid off $0.97 into a print, with an unused buyback authorisation expiring the day after. The boundary is in the price; only the four-decimal average is not.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: An actual NYSE non-compliance letter 6-K'd before or with the print, or a Q2 release announcing an ADS ratio change or reverse split, which would move this from a boundary condition to a dated corporate action.

interactions: Four real interactions. (1) WDH#0 and WDH#1 are one thesis from two sides - brokerage take-rate compression - with #0 sourced to Waterdrop's own releases and #1 to a peer's. Conditional on #0, #1 adds confirmation and no information, so scoring them as independent findings double-counts the same idea; and #0's version is strictly better evidenced because Waterdrop actually reports the line. (2) WDH#0 and WDH#2 contradict each other on the same number: #2 calls RMB639.6m an 'undisclosed revenue line' in the FY2025 20-F, while #0 correctly cites it from the 2026-03-25 press release where it was disclosed by name and carried on the wire. One of the two is wrong about the same document, and it is #2. (3) WDH#3 and WDH#4 are also one story rather than two - an unused $50m authorisation expiring 2026-09-09 is precisely the instrument a company sitting on the $1.00 listing threshold would deploy, and both claims must draw on the same piece of tape, the +2.72% five-day run-up that is entirely the 2026-09-03/04 bounce off $0.97. Whoever gets credit for that run-up, it cannot be counted twice, and the two findings point the same direction (a bid), not opposite ones. (4) WDH#2 and WDH#3 share a single published document: the 2026-08-06 Simply Wall St piece syndicated to Yahoo Finance discusses the finance-chief exit AND the buyback and semiannual dividend in the same article, so it is prior publication against both.
